name: What happens if I delay replacing damaged siding?

mainEntity.name: What happens if I delay replacing damaged siding?

acceptedAnswer.text: Delaying the replacement of damaged siding can lead to significant and costly problems. Compromised siding allows moisture to penetrate the exterior, potentially causing dry rot in the wall sheathing and structural framing. This moisture can also lead to mold growth inside the walls, which can be a health hazard. Furthermore, damaged siding reduces your home's energy efficiency, increases the risk of pest infestation, and detracts from its curb appeal and value. Addressing damage promptly prevents these issues from escalating.
acceptedAnswer.description: Delaying damaged siding replacement can cause dry rot, mold, pest infestations, reduced energy efficiency, and decreased home value. Prompt action prevents escalating damage.
